newsitem.title: UK: Saudi sugar refinery to satify 80 pct local demand.
newsitem.headline: Saudi sugar refinery to satify 80 pct local demand.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's new sugar refinery, due to start commercial production in first quarter 1997, will satisfy at least 80 percent of local demand, Muhammad Kashgari, Executive General Manager of Saudi's United Sugar Company said.

In a presentation prepared for the International Sugar Organization's London seminar on Wednesday Kashgari said the main refinery will produce 500,000 tonnes a year of high quality white sugar and will have raw sugar storage for 100,000 tonnes.
The refinery is 51 percent owned by Savola - Saudi Arabia' biggest food group, 15 percent by Britain's Tate and Lyle and the rest by Saudi sugar trading firms.
Kashgari said the refinery is more than 80 percent complete and pre-commissioning has started with the utility section.
The first shipment of raw sugar will arrive from Australia during December and USC is working with raw sugar suppliers to establish long term relationships.
United Sugar Company has signed an agreement with Tate and Lyle International to be the raw sugar purchasing agent during the initial period of operation, Kashgari said.
Saudi per capita consumption is one of the largest in the Middle East at 30 kilos per annum and all white sugar has been imported, mainly from the EU, China and Brazil.
The completion of the refinery will mean that Saudi's imports of white sugar will drop sharply and the Saudi market will become a raw sugar market.

Commenting on the global impact of the Jeddah refinery Kashgari said about half a million tonnes of white sugar will be diverted to other deficit areas, mostly in North Africa and the CIS which will eventually affect white sugar prices and supply, especially from the EU.
